facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with an enlarging purpuric patch on his left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
initially present for 2 weeks
the lesion first developed in March 2014 and was fairly stable until June 2014
rapid growth and extension followed by central ulceration and bleeding
a 30 × 25-cm centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
involving: Left anterior scalp with extension posteriorly on left parietal scalp
No evidence of lymphadenopathy in preauricular, cervical, occipital, submandibular or supraclavicular areas
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
No evidence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases
Staging: T2N0M0

concepts.why: The presence of rapid growth, ulceration, and bleeding, along with the histopathological findings of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and cells staining positively with CD31, support the diagnosis of Angiosarcoma.
The clinical presentation of multifocal, purpuric patches and papules, along with the absence of lymphadenopathy and metastases, is consistent with Kaposi's Sarcoma.
The histopathological findings of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei are consistent with Hemangioma.
The clinical presentation of a solitary, rapidly growing, purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches and papules is consistent with Pyogenic Granuloma.
The clinical presentation of multifocal, purpuric patches and papules, along with the absence of lymphadenopathy and metastases, is consistent with Bacillary Angiomatosis.
The clinical presentation of a solitary, slowly growing, purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches and papules is consistent with Dermatofibroma.
The clinical presentation of rapid growth and ulceration, along with the absence of lymphadenopathy and metastases, is consistent with Lymphoma.
The clinical presentation of multifocal, purpuric patches and papules, along with the absence of lymphadenopathy and metastases, is consistent with Leukemia Cutis.
The staging information T2N0M0, which indicates a large tumor size without lymph node involvement or metastasis, is consistent with angiosarcoma of the scalp.
